quotes.text: The Quran places kindness to parents immediately after devotion to God, and asks that we never speak to them more harshly than a sigh.
A well-known hadith holds that paradise lies at the feet of mothers — a reminder of how highly a mother's care is honored.
The Quran asks believers to lower 'the wing of humility' toward aging parents, and to pray for the mercy they once showed us as children.
Honoring your father and mother is the first of the Ten Commandments paired with a promise — that your days may be long.
Caring for one's own family, especially aging parents, is described in the New Testament as a direct mark of genuine faith.
Even from the cross, Jesus is described making sure his own mother would be cared for — a quiet model of steady filial duty.
'Matru Devo Bhava, Pitru Devo Bhava' — an ancient teaching to treat your mother and father as living forms of the divine.
In the Ramayana, Rama's devotion to honoring his father's word is held up as an ideal of filial duty.
Seva — selfless service to parents and elders — is considered one of the most direct paths to spiritual merit in Hindu tradition.
The Buddha taught that even carrying one's parents on each shoulder for a hundred years would not fully repay the debt of their care.
Caring for aging parents is framed in Buddhist teaching as compassion (karuna) practiced closest to home.
Supporting parents in their old age is named directly among a child's duties in the Buddha's teaching on family life.
Reverence for elders appears in nearly every human culture studied — not a rule imposed from outside, but something close to a universal instinct.
Caring for a parent who once cared for you is sometimes described simply as completing a circle — not a debt, but a continuation.
Caregiving is exhausting, and it's also one of the most consistently reported sources of deep meaning people describe in their lives.
You don't have to believe in anything beyond kindness itself to know that showing up for someone who once showed up for you matters.
